title: Service-level derating & autoscale interlock — contract appendix and error-budget math
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Draft an appendix to Dedicated Capacity contracts that defines a deterministic, auditable mechanics for: (1) measuring sustained throughput SLOs, (2) applying temporary derating when autoscale/fleet controls are invoked, and (3) computing customer credits from error budget burn that account for autoscale interventions and fleet-level mitigations. This doc is intended for legal + sales to include as a contract annex and for SRE/Runtime to implement measurement and reporting. It is intentionally prescriptive to minimize ambiguity during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Contract appendix text that legal approves for inclusion in standard Dedicated Capacity agreements
A2: Clear definition of derating tiers (D0..D3) and deterministic triggers mapped to autoscaler signals
A3: A formula for error-budget credit that adjusts for derating and burst allowances, expressed in tokens per-window and monthly credits
A4: Implementation acceptance tests scoped (ENG tickets) and sample telemetry dashboard queries documented
A5: Sign-off from SRE, Runtime, Sales (pricing), and Legal on wording and fallback procedures
decisions: Use time-weighted 99th-percentile sustained throughput over a rolling 30-minute window as the baseline measurement for committed throughput rather than instantaneous QPS
Derating windows invoked by autoscaler (manual or policy-triggered) will be recorded as "autoscale-interlock" events and map to discrete derating tiers
Credits computed as a function of proportionate shortfall relative to committed throughput after removing authorized derating and burst allowances
Default derating factor for D1 is 0.85 (i.e., reported serve capacity scaled to 85% when autoscale engaged for capacity-constrained events) unless customer opts into aggressive autoscale policy

2026-02-26: Legal provided redlines on notification windows and customer cure periods; incorporated required notice language

review_feedback: Legal (Maya Patel): tighten language around "authorized derating" and require 72-hour notice for non-emergency policy changes
Runtime (Ethan Park): ensure derating math can be computed from existing PromQL/Kusto queries; recommend adding a 5-minute smoothing window before recording autoscale events
SRE (Priya Nair): differentiate platform-initiated autoscale (due to AZ failures) from policy-initiated scale-downs for cost; only platform-initiated events qualify for credits
Sales (Damon Brooks): prefer a customer-visible credit estimate in invoices; asked for an example credit ledger entry format
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly generous crediting may create perverse incentives to request derating. Mitigation: cap monthly credits at 15% of committed monthly run-rate and require post-incident review before credit is applied
Risk: Measurement disputes with customer about telemetry. Mitigation: publish canonical queries and include raw time-series snapshots in incident report attachments

Risk: Autoscale false positives triggering derating. Mitigation: add 2-step confirmation where autoscale interlock must persist >10 minutes or be manually confirmed by SRE to reach higher derating tiers

example_credit_formula: Notation: C = committed throughput (tokens/sec), M = measured sustained throughput (time-weighted 99th over 30m), A = authorized derating factor (0..1), B = burst allowance in tokens/sec, T = window seconds
Shortfall S = max(0, (C - max(M, B)) * T)
Adjusted shortfall S_adj = S * (1 - A)  // removes the portion attributable to authorized derating
Monthly credit USD = min(credit_cap, S_adj * token_price_usd) where credit_cap = 0.15 * committed_monthly_bill
